en.content: Which of the following molecules, in pure form, is(are) unstable at room temperature?
en.explanation:
(a) The compound is monocyclic but non-planar due to presence of two hybridised carbon atoms. As a result, delocalisation of pi electrons (or a conjugate system) is not possible. The compound is non-aromatic.

(b) The compound is monocyclic and planar. Carbon atoms are hybridised and the pi electrons are conjugated, i.e., there is delocalisation of pi electrons. It follows electron system with electrons. This makes the compound anti-aromatic and least stable.

(c) The compound is monocyclic and planar. The carbons including carbonyl carbon are hybridised. There is no extended delocalisation of pi ( ) electrons (due to exocyclic carbonyl double bond). It also follows electron system with electrons inside the ring. This makes compound anti-aromatic and least stable.

(d) The compound is monocyclic and planar. The all carbons including carbonyl carbons are hybridised. Though, there is no extended delocalisation of electron inside the ring, but ring has electrons, i.e., electrons. This makes compound aromatic and most stable.
